content: 1. The antibiotic gemifloxacin can reduce the levels or effectiveness of estradiol by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction is specific to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and close monitoring are advised. 2. Gemifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 3. Gemifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of estropipate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction is limited to oral hormone forms, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Gemifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 5. Gemifloxacin reduces the effects of ethotoin through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are required. Additionally, quinolones have been reported to increase phenytoin levels in some cases, necessitating close monitoring. 6. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and etodolac may increase the risk of central nervous system (CNS) stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 7. Gemifloxacin and ezogabine may increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Ezogabine has been associated with slight and transient QT prolongation, especially at doses titrated to 1200 mg/day. QT interval monitoring is essential when ezogabine is prescribed with QT-prolonging agents. 8. Fennel reduces gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 9. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and fenoprofen may increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 10. Ferric citrate decreases gemifloxacin levels by binding the drug in the gastrointestinal tract. To minimize this interaction, administer gemifloxacin at least two hours before or after ferric citrate. Alternative therapies should be considered in serious cases. 11. Ferric maltol reduces gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug in serious cases. 12. Ferrous fumarate decreases gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug in serious cases. 13. Ferrous gluconate reduces gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug in serious cases. 14. Ferrous sulfate decreases gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug in serious cases. 15. Fexinidazole and gemifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole should not be combined with agents that block potassium channels or prolong the QT interval. 16. Fingolimod and gemifloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are required. 17. Gemifloxacin and flecainide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Gemifloxacin and fluconazole both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 19. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and fludrocortisone may increase the risk of tendon rupture due to the combined effects of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 20. Gemifloxacin and fluoxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 21. Gemifloxacin and fluphenazine both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are required. 22. Gemifloxacin increases flurazepam levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 23. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and flurbiprofen may increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 24. Gemifloxacin and fluvoxamine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 25. Gemifloxacin and formoterol both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are required. 26. Gemifloxacin and foscarnet both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Foscarnet has also been associated with a risk of tonic-clonic seizures. 27. Gemifloxacin reduces the effects of fosphenytoin through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are required. Quinolones have also been reported to increase phenytoin levels in some cases. 28. Gemifloxacin and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. QT prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 29. Gemifloxacin and gadobenate both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are required. 30. Gemifloxacin and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 31. Gemifloxacin and gepirone both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 32. Gemifloxacin and gilteritinib both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are required. 33. Gemifloxacin and glasdegib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for QT prolongation. 34. Gemifloxacin increases the effects of glimepiride through pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia, with gatifloxacin being the most likely to cause dysglycemia and moxifloxacin the least likely. 35. Gemifloxacin increases the effects of glipizide through pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and close monitoring are required. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia. 36. Gemifloxacin increases the effects of glyburide through pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia. 37. Goserelin increases the toxicity of gemifloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are required due to the increased risk of torsades de pointes. 38. Gemifloxacin and granisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 39. Haloperidol and gemifloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are required. 40. Histrelin increases the toxicity of gemifloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are necessary due to the increased risk of torsades de pointes. 41. Co-administration of hydrocortisone and gemifloxacin may increase the risk of tendon rupture due to the combined effects of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 42. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and gemifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 43. Gemifloxacin and hydroxyzine both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are required. 44. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and ibuprofen may increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 45. Gemifloxacin and ibutilide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 46. Gemifloxacin and iloperidone both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 47. Gemifloxacin and imipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 48. Indacaterol (inhaled) and gemifloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are required. 49. Gemifloxacin and indomethacin may increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 50.
